title: Mary Gay Scanlon addresses civil liberties, healthcare policy, and labor rights in recent posts - South Delco News
text:
Congresswoman Mary Gay Scanlon, who represents Pennsylvania’s 5th district in the U.S. Congress, recently addressed a range of policy issues on her social media account.
On December 11, 2025, Scanlon raised concerns about civil liberties and government surveillance, stating: “Americans’ most essential rights and liberties are at risk. We must protect their right to speak their minds, be free from unreasonable searches and seizures, and their essential right to privacy. The abuse of FISA by the FBI and the intelligence community must end.”
Later that day, she commented on healthcare policy: “Tick Tock. You’ve had months, and Americans can’t wait. Extend the ACA tax credits. Reverse the Medicaid cuts. Premiums won’t go through the roof.” This statement comes amid ongoing debates over federal health insurance subsidies and Medicaid funding.
On December 12, 2025, Scanlon expressed support for labor rights: “I’m proud to support our federal workers in their right to organize and bargain for fair contracts.”
Scanlon has served in Congress since 2018 after replacing Pat Meehan as representative for Pennsylvania’s 5th district. She was born in Watertown, New York in 1959 and currently resides in Swarthmore. Her educational background includes a BA from Colgate University (1980) and a JD from the University of Pennsylvania (1984).
